name: Alternate Leg Bound
description: Alternate leg bounding is an advanced plyometric drill in which the athlete performs exaggerated, explosive strides — alternating single-leg push-offs and landings across the ground with maximum stride length and height. Each stride resembles a running step taken with maximum power output. It develops unilateral explosive hip extension, stride power, and the stretch-shortening cycle in the hip extensors and plantarflexors, with strong carryover to sprinting acceleration.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a standing position. Transition to movement immediately at the start of the drill.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a flat, non-slip surface with 30–50 meters of clear running space.
steps: Step 1: Begin with a short run-up to initiate momentum.
Step 2: Drive off the right foot explosively, extending fully through the hip, knee, and ankle.
Step 3: Drive the left knee high and forward while the right arm mirrors with an aggressive drive.
Step 4: Land on the left foot and immediately drive off again with equal force.
Step 5: Continue alternating for the prescribed distance, maximizing each stride's length and height.
common_mistakes: Shuffling rather than bounding — each stride must be a true explosive effort
Insufficient knee lift of the swing leg
Weak arm drive — the arms contribute significantly to stride power
safety_considerations: High demand on the Achilles tendon and hamstrings. Not appropriate in the early season or after lower limb injury.
Progress from single-leg hops before adding alternate leg bounds.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Maximum stride length and height. Full hip and knee extension at each takeoff.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Performed for 20–40 meter sets. Maximum effort on each stride.
coaching_cues: Drive the knee up and push the ground away
Swing the arms hard — opposite arm to leg
